title: A task that raises Ignore sends no event after task-started: a monitor built on events.State (Flower) shows it STARTED for ever, also when the task stored SUCCESS by hand as tasks.rst shows
where: request.py:704-705 (celery 768e476, the same at 9c2f238): on_failure with Ignore only acknowledges the message; no task event follows task-started (request.py:525-533). tasks.rst:1489-1522 says Ignore records no state and shows update_state(SUCCESS) then raise Ignore as the way to store a result by hand; monitoring.rst:719-748 lists task-succeeded and task-failed as the events after task-started and has no event for an ignored task. Reject(requeue=False) had the same gap in the backend and was given a FAILURE in celery issue 4222's fix (request.py:680-703); Ignore was not. No upstream thread found (searched Ignore flower STARTED, task-ignored event, raise Ignore event, Ignore exception flower, Ignore task stays started, Ignore task-succeeded in celery issues and pull requests; Ignore STARTED, task ignored started, Ignore exception in mher/flower issues; closest celery issue 4222, Reject keeps a task STARTED, closed, and flower issue 1361, Task is ignored, about fast tasks not shown); not in the tracker yet
thread: none yet (a new issue, or a docs sentence in tasks.rst's Ignore section; the lead decides)
observed: 9c2f238 with kombu 445027e, redis-py 8.1.0, Redis 7 broker and backend, one prefork worker -c 2 -E, a monitor feeding every event into app.events.State; nothing injected. ignore: 3 of 3 runs the events were task-received and task-started, events.State showed STARTED 4 s later, the backend PENDING. updateignore (update_state(SUCCESS) then Ignore): 3 of 3 the same events, events.State STARTED, the backend SUCCESS. Control returns: 3 of 3 task-succeeded, SUCCESS on both sides. Celery 5.5.3 and 5.4.0: updateignore 1 of 1 each the same. Flower itself was not run; it keeps its task states in events.State. Natural rate: every task that raises Ignore with events enabled; no timing involved. The same script's case hard (time_limit=1, a 5 s sleep): 3 of 3 two task-failed events on 9c2f238 (finding hard-limit-twice), one on 5.5.3 and 5.4.0 (1 of 1 each).
